decisions.reason: Uses host-input-contract.ts (Occurrence offset/length and InputState.draft are clipboard-text projection, chips expanded to clipboardText) and host-input-facade.ts (TokenSpan and $replaceDetectSpanWith* operate on detectText, chip = exactly one U+FFFC) to state the two coordinate systems and that ordinary text keeps its normal width in both.

Locates snapshot.draft.length as the span source in plugin-client.js add, explains that with an initially empty composer the projections coincide so paste #1 applies, while after the first chip the clipboard length (29) overshoots the 2-char detect span so the splice fails and insertReference returns false, which the plugin converts into its changed-composer toast; correctly treats the toast as deterministic mismatch, not a real concurrent edit, and derives the counts from the capture rather than asserting inconsistent hardcoded values.

Traces remove(): clipboard-projection occurrence.offset/length passed unconverted as the consumeToken span against the detect text, the false result never inspected, and records.delete(ref) running unconditionally; the live occurrence keeps the dock and composer chips while the missing record renders 'unavailable' per the dock excerpt — both symptoms tied to the single coordinate mismatch rather than a separate upload failure.

Derives and applies the conversion at both call sites: detectDelta = occurrence.length − 1 per preceding chip; insertion at draft end uses draft.length minus the sum over all occurrences; removal maps occurrence.offset to a one-detect-character span [detectStart, detectStart+1); keeps the draftRev guard (re-reading the snapshot after edits) and retires records only after consumeToken reports success, noting the clipboard-coordinate setDraft fallback is dimensionally correct.

Proposes two successive pastes asserting both occurrences/chips, byte-size dock meta and no toast, then removal with another chip present asserting the target's composer occurrence, dock chip and record disappear together while the other chip survives and re-based offsets stay consistent; adds empty-again, declined-consumption and invariant assertions (span width 1, records size equals occurrences length).
